title: Adhesion and standardized contracts
summary: An adhesion contract is a standardized agreement presented by a party with superior bargaining power on terms the other party can generally accept or reject rather than negotiate.
notes:
Graham shows that even an experienced businessperson may face an adhesive form when industry arrangements leave no realistic alternative. The label begins the inquiry; it does not itself decide that every term is unenforceable. The court separately considered reasonable expectations and an arbitrator’s structural bias.

Other readings examine notice of terms, the duty to read, consumer statutes, and substantive unfairness. Klar turns on the meaning and notice of a claim check. Doe applies a statute regulating a particular service. Anderson addresses attempted adoption and retroactive use of changed online terms. These are separate legal mechanisms for assessing standardized contracting. The course-wide index preserves those differences.
